shape.text: A service account token begins with the literal prefix ops_. The provider's security page says the prefix was chosen to help code analyzers recognize the token.
The rest of the token is a serialized JSON object encoded as Base64url, so the body begins eyJ, the Base64 of an opening brace and quote.

The documented encoding is Base64url (letters, digits, underscore and hyphen), with optional equals padding at the end. Every sample seen contains only letters and digits after the prefix. A standard-Base64 plus or slash is outside the documented class, although one scanner rule uses the standard class.
Length is variable by construction. The provider's one encoded example is 634 characters and begins ops_eyJ; values observed in the research range from 634 to 870 characters.
A real token has at least 250 Base64url characters after ops_eyJ.

unresolved.reason: The provider states no minimum length; a floor of 250 Base64url characters after the prefix is a project choice that matches one scanner's floor.

issuance.text: A service account hands automation its token through the OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN environment variable, which the command-line tool and the SDKs read.
No 1Password service account token was issued or observed for this record.

unresolved.reason: No service account token was issued for this research.

collisions.text: The Connect server token (OP_CONNECT_TOKEN) is a different credential: a standard three-segment JWT.
Secret references of the form op://vault/item/field point at a secret and are not themselves secrets.
The account Secret Key (the A3- form) is a separate credential with its own grammar.

unresolved.reason: The grammar of the account Secret Key has not been researched; only a research note records that it is a separate credential.

openQuestions.text: Does the serialization produced by the web dashboard differ in length or alphabet from the command-line serialization?

unresolved.reason: A difference has been reported but not confirmed; no issued dashboard token and CLI token were compared.
